title: Inside Publishing’s Big Shakeup: AI, TikTok & the Battle Ahead | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 34

metadata.title: Inside Publishing’s Big Shakeup: AI, TikTok & the Battle Ahead | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 34

summary: A publishing panel explains changes in discovery, editorial labor, rights and author compensation, with Eisman mainly asking questions. The material themes are platform dependence, AI substitution of generic information, differentiated author brands and licensing economics. Verified corrections concern Amazon's generated-content policy, the distinction between training and piracy in Bartz, and author-funded costs hidden by headline hybrid royalty comparisons.
assessment: Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts literary agents Regina Brooks and Jennifer Weis, and publisher Anthony Ziccardi. Unclear overlapping turns are explicitly marked uncertain.
framework_points: Follow distribution and discovery power as formats change.
Separate generic information from differentiated author voice and community.
Do not infer legal infringement merely from technical model training.
Compare net contract economics after author-funded costs and rights grants.
Use portfolio economics for hit-driven creative businesses.
Historical data can screen out ideas with no close precedent.
tools_and_charts: Print, ebook and audio revenue versus unit shares
Advance, royalty and author-funded cost comparison
Training rights versus output and acquisition rights
transcript_cautions: Panel overlaps create uncertain attribution on some interjections; those are excluded from Eisman scoring.
ASR spells Jennifer Weis and Anthony Ziccardi inconsistently; names normalized.
Opening montage repeats body claims and differs on the unverified author-AI-use percentage.
Literary anecdotes, plot judgments and incidental author-name/date slips are omitted as immaterial.
Revenue data cannot directly grade the panel's illustrative unit mix.

assumptions: Approval requires favorable data from closely comparable prior products.

evidence_basis.proof: A project without comparable history cannot satisfy the historical-comparable requirement even if its eventual quality or demand is high. The rule can therefore exclude novelty.

evidence.title: Bartz v Anthropic order on fair use, document 231
evidence.publisher: U.S. District Court, N.D. California; copy hosted by Loeb
evidence.finding: Court distinguished transformative model training from acquisition and retention of pirated books. Training use received summary judgment; pirated library copies were not excused by that later use.

evidence.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence initiative
evidence.finding: Office issued reports addressing digital replicas, copyrightability and generative-AI training. Copyright in human authorship and licensing/fair-use questions require separate analysis; policy study is not a blanket court judgment.

evidence.title: Bartz settlement FAQ

assumptions: Title-level profits are uneven and some losses occur.
Profits on successful titles exceed aggregate losses on unsuccessful titles.
evidence_basis.proof: Total portfolio profit is the sum of title profits and losses, so the portfolio can be profitable even when many titles lose money.
